from_source_gfx1201.base: Prism d8f26eec76da6d09bb708bcba51ef64b8cd868a3 (prism branch) + 12-line qwen35.cpp MTP-embedding Hadamard patch

from_source_vs_prebuilt_nonspec.conclusion: A gfx1201-only from-source build does not meaningfully beat the prebuilt. The prebuilt is already fine for raw throughput.

mtp.prebuilt_rejection: llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: Hadamard-latent table 'token_embd.weight' is read without the inverse transform

qwen_mtp_reference.note: The older b10472 Vulkan build measured q8_0/q8_0 at 262k at 20-23 t/s; b10902 fixes it. The user's 45-46 t/s claim is real (and conservative).

head_to_head_262k_q8q8_mtp.conclusion: With MTP, Bonsai 2 beats Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K by 1.24-1.66x at 262k while using 61% vs 99% of the card.

perplexity_same_corpus_ctx4096_5chunks.caveat: Bonsai measured on ROCm, Qwen on Vulkan; backend ppl effect is typically <1%, so the gap is quantization loss.

capability_suites_chat_ctx32768.conclusion: Tied on pass/fail suites; the 27.5% perplexity gap is the sensitive signal. Bonsai does not preserve Q6_K quality.

ninfer_bespoke.ninfer_status: CUDA-only, hard-coded sm_120a (RTX 5090). No AMD/HIP/ROCm port, branch, or PR.
ninfer_bespoke.from_scratch_effort: 6+ months to parity; NInfer took ~3 months on a mature CUDA stack

r9700_options.ZINC: https://github.com/zolotukhin/zinc - Vulkan+ROCm, measured on one R9700, beats llama.cpp ~7-8% decode and up to 1.9x prefill
r9700_options.R9V: https://github.com/Dyluhn/R9V - shape-specialized gfx1201 kernels, dual-R9700, experimental, MTP4
r9700_options.vllm_radiance: single-R9700 vLLM fork, MXFP4 + MTP, 137.7 t/s combined decode (needs MXFP4/FP8 weights, no safetensors on the mount)
r9700_options.Zynfer: https://github.com/thanos/zynfer - NInfer-inspired Zig, R9700 target, Phase R not yet running

ninfer_bespoke.conclusion: NInfer itself is not portable to the R9700. The pragmatic path is ZINC (R9700-native, beats llama.cpp) or the radiance vLLM fork, not a from-scratch engine. llama.cpp already sits near the decode bandwidth wall.
